newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Defiant Gaddafi gets Nigeria's top honour.
newsitem.headline: Defiant Gaddafi gets Nigeria's top honour.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, who defied a U.N. ban on flights from his country by flying to Niger and Nigeria, was bestowed Nigeria's highest honour medal, state radio said on Saturday.
Gaddafi was decorated with the medal of Grand Commander of the Federal Republic of Nigeria by military ruler General Sani Abacha at a state banquet in Abuja on Friday night.
A similar honour medal was granted to President Ibrahim Bare Mainnasara of Niger, who accompanied Gaddafi on his trip to Nigeria.
Both men, who like their host are shunned by the West, flew in to Kano in northern Nigeria on Friday for the Moslem prayers.
Gaddafi told a large crowd of worshippers in Kano that the West was tarnishing the image of Islam by portraying it as a terrorist movement.
Gaddafi's trip to West Africa is in apparent defiance of a 1992 United Nations embargo on flights from his pariah state.
The ban was imposed for Libya's failure to extradite two agents linked to the bombing of the Pan Am flight over Lockerbie in 1988 and four agents linked to the 1989 bombing of a French airliner.
"The sanctions on Libya, Iraq, Iran were not imposed by the true United Nations. They were imposed by the United States and the Atlantic Alliance who are against Islam," Gaddafi said.

In Washington, a State Department spokesman said on Thursday the United States was investigating reports that the flight embargo had been broken and if it had been, the matter would be pursued in the U.N. Security Council and sanctions committee. A U.S. official said military action was not being considered.
Gaddafi's last trip abroad was by land to Tunisia in October 1996. He violated the ban when a Libyan-registered plane flew him to Cairo and back to attend an Arab summit in June 1996.
State radio said the Libyan leader would "summit talks" in Abuja with Abacha before leaving later on Saturday.
